newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss mull new name for liberalised telecoms unit.
newsitem.headline: Swiss mull new name for liberalised telecoms unit.

text.p: Switzerland's state telecommunications provider will decide next week on a new name for itself as it braces to face competiton in a liberalised market next year, it said on Friday.
Parliament approved in principle on Thursday a package of legislation that overhauls the state Post, Telephone and Telegraph authority (PTT) and will partially privatise telecommunications in 1998.
Final approval, considered a formality, is set for April.
The legislation splits the PTT into two separate units. Telecommunications activities will be transformed into a joint stock company, with the Swiss government holding a majority.

The goal is to sell a minority stake in Swiss Telecom so that the company could be listed in the second half of 1998. The postal authority will remain a state-owned agency without benefit of cross-subsidy from the telecoms arm.

"Today our name is Telecom PTT, but after the split the PTT part will be dropped and you cannot legally protect the name Telecom, so that would be a poor solution," Telecom PTT spokesman Sepp Huber said.
Known internationally as Swiss Telecom, the company faces the identity problem only domestically.
The legislation passed this week requires competitors entering the Swiss market to respect prevailing working conditions in the telecoms sector.
This was adopted to reassure trade unions that competition would not undercut wages. Unions had threatened to mount a referendum drive to block the reforms.
"It is rather unlikely now that it will come to a referendum," Huber said.
The reform is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 1998, in line with the European Union's liberalisation of its telecommuncations market.

Switzerland took a first step to loosening its telecommunications law in 1991, letting private companies offer some kinds of data transmission. But the PTT still holds a monopoly over most voice transmission and the cellular network.
